title: Color System Studio — Accessible OKLCH Palettes
description: Build an accessible design-token palette: pick brand hues and chroma, and each palette becomes an eleven-step 50–950 ramp generated in OKLCH and converted to sRGB with real gamut clipping. A WCAG contrast matrix grades every text-on-background pair, light and dark previews of a sample UI run their own contrast checks, and the whole system exports as CSS custom properties or JSON design tokens.
prompt: Build 'Color System Studio', an accessible design-token palette builder. Let me pick brand hues, generate 50–950 ramps in OKLCH — implement the OKLCH → OKLab → linear sRGB conversion yourself, with gamut clipping that reduces chroma while keeping lightness and hue, and flag the steps that were clipped. Add a WCAG contrast matrix of text-on-background pairs with real ratios and AA / AA-large / AAA badges, a light and dark preview of a small sample UI built from semantic tokens with pass/fail checks, and export as CSS custom properties or JSON tokens (hex or oklch notation). Persist my palettes. Keep the page itself Swiss and nearly colourless — black rules, big grotesque type, one red accent — so the palette is the only colour that matters.

methodology: Reference values for the colour maths: OKLCH coordinates of pure sRGB red, CSS green, mid grey, white and black must convert to exactly #ff0000, #008000, #808080, #ffffff and #000000.
Independent oracle for contrast: the spec carries its own WCAG 2 luminance and ratio implementation and checks a full matrix row, cell by cell, against the page's ratios and badges.
Gamut-boundary property test: the clipped chroma must be in gamut while chroma + 0.002 is out — proving the binary search lands on the sRGB edge rather than clipping arbitrarily.
Monotonicity and format invariants: every ramp has eleven valid hex values whose luminance strictly decreases from 50 to 950.
Behavioural checks on the semantic layer: the defaults pass all light and dark checks, and a bright yellow primary still yields a readable on-primary label.
Export round-trip: the JSON export is parsed in the test, palettes and semantic tokens are verified, and a renamed palette survives a reload.
risks: Rounding at the AA threshold: ratios are truncated (not rounded) to two decimals for display so a 4.495 never shows as a passing 4.50.
Contrast is computed from the 8-bit hex that ships, not the unrounded float colour, otherwise the badge could disagree with the exported token.
Re-rendering the palette while a range slider is being dragged would drop the pointer; only the ramp and outputs are patched in place during input.
qa.playwright: This page is maths-heavy, so the spec leans on oracles instead of screenshots: known conversion values evaluated through a small window.__color hook, and an independent WCAG implementation inside the test file to recompute ratios from the data-fg/data-bg attributes on each matrix cell. Sliders are set with locator.fill(), which fires input events on range controls. The gamut test checks a property (inside at the boundary, outside just beyond it) rather than a magic chroma number, so it stays valid if the ramp's lightness curve is tuned. Colour is never judged from pixels.
coverage: Ramp validity, darkening order, hue slider effect and export sync
Gamut clipping at high chroma, none at low chroma, boundary property
Contrast matrix ratios and grades against an independent WCAG oracle
Light and dark semantic checks; on-primary label selection
CSS and JSON export, oklch notation, add and rename palette, reload persistence

a11y: Every slider and field is labelled, swatches are buttons named with their step, hex value and clip status, and the contrast matrix is a real table with row and column headers inside a keyboard-scrollable region. Grades are text badges (AAA, AA, AA LG, FAIL), never colour alone.
